sources.title: CTF skills
sources.author: Lukasz Jagiello and contributors
principles: category-specific technique catalogs with a short entrypoint
reviewed scripts and tool references
symptom-based routing
local_implementation: preserved reverse/pwn imports at the e79be292 pin
new references and scripts are independently written or retain their upstream notice
category entrypoints rewritten for portable Agent Skills hosts
sources.notes: Between e79be292 and a16e19a only evals/package-lock.json and evals/package.json changed. No new skill content was available to integrate. The upstream pwnable.tw writeup tree and ctf-misc/audio.md were reviewed; local references already cover their primitives, so no duplicate import was made. ctf-similar-search remains rejected for exact-solution retrieval and an external API key.

sources.title: opencode-for-ctf
sources.author: h1kibi and contributors
principles: FAST and EXPERT lanes
evidence-first closure with candidate versus oracle-verified states
explicit phase and route budgets
thin category controllers with lazy references
local_implementation: FAST/EXPERT selection in ctf-common and plan_solve.py
candidate provenance and verification ledger in ctf-common and ctf_state.py
bounded hypothesis and payload-family budgets
short category entrypoints with symptom indexes
sources.notes: The plugin runtime, agents, MCP tools and TeamProbe orchestration are not required or copied; this repository stays standalone.

sources.title: D-CIPHER multi-agent CTF solver
sources.author: Udeshi et al.; NYU-LLM-CTF
principles: separate planning from execution
explicit evaluation of each task result
environment feedback changes the next step
local_implementation: one-test-at-a-time loop in ctf-common/references/workflow.md
failure-layer classification and progress check
compact state/hypothesis templates
sources.notes: No planner/executor agent hierarchy is required; the same discipline is expressed as a compact solving contract.

sources.title: EnIGMA: Interactive Tools Substantially Assist LM Agents in Finding Security Vulnerabilities
sources.author: Abramovich et al.
sources.license: arXiv paper license; no text copied
principles: interactive debugger and terminal tools materially help
persistent tool state and grounded observations
models can self-generate hallucinated observations
local_implementation: interactive tool ladder in references/tooling.md and category skills
state ledger separates observations from inference
verification requires observed output, not model narration
sources.notes: No debugger runtime is bundled. The skills prefer scripted non-interactive tool use and only describe interactive workflows when available.

sources.title: Measuring and Augmenting Large Language Models for Solving Capture-the-Flag Challenges
sources.author: Ji, Wu, Jiang, Ma, Li and Wang
sources.license: project page CC BY-SA 4.0; paper/source access is separate
principles: technical retrieval helps, but application to the specific scenario is the bottleneck
environment feedback and adaptation matter more than static knowledge
two-stage retrieval can narrow techniques before action
local_implementation: symptom indexes plus lookup_knowledge.py for targeted retrieval
cheap discriminator and failure-layer adaptation
research only when the current model is insufficient
sources.notes: CTFAgent source is gated; no code or prompt was copied.

sources.title: PentestGPT
sources.author: GreyDGL and contributors
principles: durable task state
phased problem solving
tool leases and explicit progress tracking
local_implementation: STATE.md/HYPOTHESES.md and evidence.jsonl
recovery after compaction or instance refresh
bounded branch budgets
sources.notes: No task-lease runtime or agent backend is bundled.

sources.title: CTFusion: A CTF-based Benchmark for LLM Agent Evaluation
sources.author: Lee, Bae and Yun; KAIST HackingLab
principles: fair A/B comparisons need independent environments
track per-agent results and flag provenance
live evaluation reduces contamination but needs scope discipline
local_implementation: deterministic skill/route/prompt tests
docs/EVALUATION.md describes an optional A/B/C model protocol
no CTFd, platform submission or live-competition automation is included
sources.notes: No comparative model run was performed for this overhaul.

sources.title: AgentLSD: Evaluating AI Security Agents Under Adversarial Task Contamination
sources.author: Golinelli, Drago, Boffa, Bergadano and Crispo
sources.license: arXiv paper license; no text or trap implementation copied
principles: task contamination includes non-instructional false evidence, not only prompt injection
trap families: goal hijack, false authority, false validation, exploration bait, time sink
traps increase turns and reasoning tokens even when the flag is still found
preserve provenance and require independent evidence before accepting success
local_implementation: ctf-common/references/adversarial-content.md trap protocol
scan_untrusted.py advisory scanner
candidate origin and verification ledger
explicit decoy budget and intended-task preservation
sources.notes: Finite deterministic tests do not establish universal trap immunity; the scanner is heuristic and advisory.

sources.title: How Do LLM Agents Actually Get the Flag? Trace-Level Provenance for Agentic Offensive Security Evaluation
sources.author: Milner et al.
sources.license: arXiv paper license; no text or code copied
principles: flag provenance matters: intended exploit, exposure, recall, lookup, guess or unsupported claim
recovered flags are not all demonstrated exploitation
record where the value first appeared and what action produced it
local_implementation: verification provenance ladder
candidate origin labels and first-appearance note
reporting distinguishes checker/derivation/runtime/static/model
optional trace fields in ctf_state.py
sources.notes: The skills do not claim that a recovered flag implies the intended exploit.

sources.title: Refusal in Language Models Is Mediated by a Single Direction
sources.author: Arditi, Obeso, Syed, Paleka, Panickssery, Gurnee and Nanda
sources.license: arXiv paper license; no text or method copied
principles: refusal behavior is brittle in studied open models
white-box activation work is a research topic, not a CTF-solving shortcut
local_implementation: treated only as background in docs/RESEARCH.md
sources.notes: No abliteration, refusal bypass, provider-control evasion or capability claim is implemented. CTF analysis of authorized malicious artifacts is handled by instruction-source separation, not by disabling model safety.

sources.title: PRESTIGE
sources.author: 0xAldoLim
principles: evidence before confidence
FAST to EXPERT escalation
candidate verification separate from model assertion
operator-controlled scope and budgets
local_implementation: standalone solving contract and state ledger
no runtime dependency, MCP server, Docker or model gateway
sources.notes: PRESTIGE is not required to install or use these skills. Its working tree was not modified.

sources.title: HackSynth: LLM Agent and Evaluation Framework for Autonomous Penetration Testing
sources.author: Muzsai, Imolai and Lukacs
principles: planner and summarizer modules with iterative command feedback
explicit benchmark and budget configuration
separate command generation from feedback reduction
local_implementation: compact observation summaries and one-test-at-a-time loop
explicit budgets and state checkpoints
sources.notes: The paper is arXiv:2412.01778. AGPL code was not copied; only the general planner/summarizer and feedback-loop idea was considered.

sources.title: How Vulnerable Are AI Agents to Indirect Prompt Injections? Insights from a Large-Scale Public Competition
sources.author: Dziemian et al.; Gray Swan AI and collaborators
sources.license: arXiv paper license; no text or attack implementation copied
principles: indirect prompt injection in tool-calling, coding and computer-use agents
concealment: a successful attack may leave no clue in the final user-facing response
inspect tool actions and side effects, not only the final answer
local_implementation: adversarial protocol checks side effects and tool calls
verification requires observed action/support, not a clean final message
agent-security reference maps write/read boundaries and canaries
sources.notes: Gray Swan's public research page was reviewed; no attack payloads or benchmark data were copied.
